findings.text: under -q, including the repository's own declared -q -n form, pytest suppresses both the "collected N items" line and the xdist "[N items]" form, so _collected at :114 returns None and collection_failed collapses to exit_status != 0: a project whose single test runs and fails is recorded collected=null, failed=1, collection_failed=true and hold_reason at :350 then takes the same branch as a true collection failure and reports the run as having failed to collect (measured: review-logs/measure-counts.log; the same suite without -q records collected=1 and collection_failed=false), so the distinction the fragment states at docs/evidence/fragments/a-review-is-sized-to-its-risk/the-suite-is-declared-and-recorded.html:93 - a failing suite is not a suite that stopped running - does not hold for the command the project declares, and collected, a count the goal names, is unmeasurable in that form.

every hold case builds a suite that cannot be collected (a syntax error) or one that passes; no case runs a suite that collects, runs and fails, so the misclassification above never reaches the gate and the collection branch is exercised for the true collection failure alone.

the two-argument hold_reason(project_root, tier) the done_when names resolves its project by mounting at :362 and returns None when the root's docs tree is not itself a mount, even while the latest record carries collection_failed: measured on a throwaway project, hold_reason(root, "none") returns None while hold_reason(root, "none", "proj") returns the hold sentence (review-logs/measure-counts-forms.log:211-214), so a checkout run outside the mount table - a worktree, a clone, a project under test - silently receives no hold rather than an error.

the done_when requires the record to be written through a writer that already exists in reckon/_store.py; no such writer exists at this revision, and record() writes through a call-time import of reckon.crew.runs._write_json instead - disclosed in the manifest and the fragment, and atomic, but the clause reads false to a reader checking the done-when literally and the record's durability now depends on a private helper in another package.
